html:
Bulgaria is a country in the eastern Balkans, between the Danube and the Black Sea. The modern state appears on the map from 1880, two years after it was carved out of the Ottoman Empire.

Its roots are much older. The Bulgars, a Turkic people from the steppe, settled south of the Danube in 681 and merged with the Slavs there. The state turned Christian in 864, and its scholars spread the Cyrillic alphabet to the Slavic world. Medieval Bulgaria rivalled the Byzantine Empire twice, then fell to the Ottomans in 1396 for almost five hundred years.

The modern state:

  • 1878: after a Russian war against the Ottomans, the Congress of Berlin created a small self governing principality.
  • 1885: it united with Eastern Rumelia to the south.
  • 1908: it declared full independence, with a tsar.
  • 1912 to 1913: it won and then lost land in the Balkan Wars.
  • It fought on the losing side in both world wars.

In 1944 the Soviet army arrived and a communist government took power. Todor Zhivkov ruled from 1954 to 1989, and Bulgaria was among the closest allies of the Soviet Union. After 1989 it became a parliamentary republic. It joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007, together with Romania.
sum: Bulgaria is a country in the eastern Balkans, between the Danube and the Black Sea. The modern state appears on the map from 1880, two years after it was carved out of the Ottoman Empire.
